interface.signature: def checkMirrorTree(n: int, e: int, A: list, B: list) -> int

preconditions.description: The number of nodes n and edges e are within the specified constraints.
Arrays A and B each contain exactly 2*e integers representing e edges.

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= u <= n and 1 <= v <= n for u, v in zip(A[::2], A[1::2])) and all(1 <= u <= n and 1 <= v <= n for u, v in zip(B[::2], B[1::2]))
preconditions.description: All edge endpoints in both arrays are valid node indices between 1 and n.
Both edge lists define trees containing all n nodes (implied by tree structure with n nodes and n-1 edges, though e is given as n-1 implicitly for a tree).

postconditions.description: The function returns either 1 (mirror images) or 0 (not mirror images).

postconditions.expression: return_value == 1 if (sorted([(u, tuple(sorted(children_a))) for u, children_a in adj_a.items()]) == sorted([(u, tuple(sorted(children_b))) for u, children_b in adj_b.items()]) and all(adj_a[u] == list(reversed(adj_b[u])) for u in adj_a)) else 0
postconditions.description: Returns 1 if and only if the two trees have identical node sets and for every node, the list of children in the first tree is the reverse of the list of children in the second tree (assuming consistent ordering of children in the input representation), otherwise returns 0. Note: This assumes the input arrays define a rooted tree structure where parent-child relationships are consistent and the 'mirror' property holds for the specific ordering of children implied by the input sequence.
